records.label: Family NNO-SA1
records.segregation: single novel missense variant segregating with disease in the linked region
quotes: Of the 35 available individuals from family NNO-SA1, 16 participants (46%) had a diagnosis of nanophthalmos, with mean refraction of +11.8 D and mean axial length of 17.6 mm.
Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region located in exon 8 of the transmembrane-98 (TMEM98) gene c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro)

notes.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) found that a 20.2-Mb segment of chromosome 17p12-q12 (rs530664-rs16523) cosegregated with nanophthalmos in pedigree 991-F and an overlapping 19.7-Mb segment (rs917541-rs16523) in pedigree 951-N, placing the disease gene between rs917541 and rs16523, overlapping a region previously linked in a Chinese pedigree.
quotes: In pedigree 991-F, a 20.2 Mbp segment of chromosome 17p12-q12, bounded by SNPs rs530664 and rs16523, was transmitted with nanophthalmos in all members of the family.
These data suggest that the gene that causes autosomal dominant nanophthalmos in pedigrees 991-F and 951-N lies between SNPs rs917541 and rs16523 on chromosome 17 (Figure 3).

notes.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) identified a His196Pro missense mutation in TMEM98 by exome sequencing in a US pedigree and a heterozygous 34-bp deletion spanning the exon 4/intron 4 splice junction in a Mariana Islands pedigree with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos; both cosegregated with disease, were absent from public databases, and affected conserved sequences. The deletion was predicted to eliminate a splice site and cause premature termination.
quotes: This TMEM98 deletion eliminates a splice site and results in a premature termination of translation.
Neither the His196Pro mutation nor the 34 bp deletion was detected in public DNA sequence databases including the Exome Variation Server and the 1000 Genomes Project.

notes.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) reported that affected members of the US pedigree had mean axial length 17.1 mm and high hyperopia (about +13 D), whereas affected members of the Pacific Islander pedigree had mean axial length 17.4 mm but lesser hyperopia (+3.93 D); both pedigrees showed autosomal dominant inheritance with high penetrance over at least 4 generations.
quotes: Both pedigrees exhibit an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with high penetrance that spans at least four generations.
Along with short axial eye lengths, family members with nanophthalmos also had hyperopia with spherical equivalent refractions of +3.93±1.57 diopters.

notes.statement: In a large white family with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos (NNO-SA1), Awadalla et al. (2014) found significant linkage to chromosome 17 between SNP markers rs2323659 and rs967293, with a maximum location score of 4.1.
quotes: Significant linkage was detected on chromosome 17 between single-nucleotide polymorphism markers rs2323659 and rs967293, with a maximum location score of 4.1.

notes.statement: Awadalla et al. (2014) found the TMEM98 c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro) variant absent from the Exome Variant Server database and from 285 local white controls. They concluded that TMEM98 most likely represented the cause of disease in this family, and described it as the first gene identified causing autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.
quotes: which was absent in the Exome Variant Server database and among 285 local white individuals serving as controls
TMEM98 most likely represents the cause of the disease in this family. To our knowledge, this represents the first gene identified causing autosomal dominant nanophthalmos.

notes.statement: By RT-PCR, Awadalla et al. (2014) found TMEM98 expressed in all ocular tissues tested, including sclera and optic nerve head.
quotes: The TMEM98 gene was expressed in all ocular tissues tested including sclera and optic nerve head.

notes.statement: In a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital simple microphthalmia, Hu et al. (2011) performed a genomewide scan and obtained a maximum lod score of 4.97 at D17S1824 (theta = 0.00). Haplotype analysis placed the disease locus in a 21.57-cM interval between D17S900 and D17S1872 on chromosome 17p12-q12.
quotes: The most statistically significant linkage results were obtained at D17S1824 (maximum LOD score, 4.97, at recombination fraction 0.00).
Haplotype analyses supported the location of the disease-causing gene to a 21.57-cM interval between loci D17S900 and D17S1872 of chromosome 17, region p12-q12.

notes.statement: Hu et al. (2011) screened 14 candidate genes in the linked region, including CRYBA1 and NCOR1, and performed genomewide SNP genotyping, but identified no mutation or copy number variation responsible for the microphthalmia phenotype in the family.
quotes: 14 candidate genes including CRYBA1 and NCOR1 were selected to screen for the mutation by the PCR direct-sequencing method.
However, no mutation or CNV (copy number variation) was identified to be responsible for the microphthalmia phenotype of this pedigree.

notes.statement: Yu et al. (2009) reported a 5-generation Chinese family in which 9 members aged 6 to 66 years had isolated bilateral microphthalmia from birth, with hyperopia of +4.50 to +11.50 diopters (mean +8.00) and axial length of 18.22 to 20.26 mm (mean 19.29 mm). Angle-closure glaucoma or occludable angles occurred in 3 patients older than 50 years and progressed despite trabeculectomy, and 2 developed atrophia bulbi. Learning disabilities were seen in one-third of cases.
quotes: Combined hyperopia ranged from +4.50 to +11.50 diopters (mean: +8.00 diopters). The axial length was from 18.22 mm to 20.26 mm (mean: 19.29 mm), which was shorter than the normal length of 23–24 mm.

Angle-closure glaucoma or occludable anterior chamber angles were present in three patients who were all older than 50 years of age and was treated by trabeculectomy, but the pathogenetic condition kept developing.
Learning disabilities were observed in one-third of the cases.

notes.statement: Yu et al. (2009) found on histology of the sclera diffusely swollen, twisted or frayed collagen fibers mixed with normal fibers. In atrophied globes, collagen alignment was disrupted, the sclera was about 3 times normal thickness, and pigment cell proliferation and bone-like tissue were seen.
quotes: The diffusely swelled collagen fibers were twisted or frayed and were mixed with normal fibers (Figure 2A).
the alignment of collagen fibers was disrupted and there were a lot of coil-like amorphic materials in the scleras with three times the thickness of a normal sclera.

notes.statement: In a Chinese family with autosomal dominant microphthalmia, Yu et al. (2009) excluded linkage to the known candidate genes (CHX10, PAX6, MFRP) and loci (14q32, 11p, 2q11-q14), with LOD scores below 1 for all 23 markers tested. They predicted that a novel locus was responsible.
quotes: a LOD score of less than 1 with all 23 markers involved did not support any linkage relation in this study, so we excluded the linkage of microphthalmia in this pedigree with the reported candidate genes (CHX10, PAX6, and MFRP) and loci (chromosomes 14q32, 11p, and 2q11-q14).
A novel locus is predicted to be responsible for the microphthalmia in this family.
